notes: Account overview: Valencia Orbit builds a multi-tenant inference platform used by fintech and retail partners; evaluating Dedicated pools to guarantee latency and throughput for customer-facing chat + personalization lanes.
Primary ask: guaranteed reserved GPU capacity across 3 regions (us-east1, us-west2, eu-west1) with failover headroom; explicit throughput SLOs at peak and predictable cold-start behavior.
Workloads: chat (conversational agent front-end), reranking for search results, embeddings for semantic search; peak patterns 09:00-11:00 and 17:00-19:00 PST for US customers; EU peak offset.
Throughput targets: 1,200 concurrent RPS (chat requests/sec) with batching expected; target sustained throughput 900 req/s per region during business hours.
Latency SLOs: p50 < 40ms token gen / p95 end-to-end <= 120ms for short-chat (<256 tokens); reranking p95 <= 80ms; embeddings p99 <= 200ms.

GPU sizing ask: equivalent of 12 H100 units spread across 3 regions (nominal allocation 4 H100-eq/region) with 30% failover headroom for single-region outage and extra burst capacity for marketing events.
Failover strategy discussed: active-passive cross-region routing + prefetched KV cache replication for hottest prefixes; questions about cache warm-up time and cross-region consistency.
Model plan: primary model is open-llama-70B-quant for chat; fallback to 13B quant when latency spikes; need routing policy to prefer dedicated pool but fallback to hosted API for extended outages.

Billing/commit: looking for 12–36 month reserved contract options; prefer blended rate for committed capacity + per-token overage billing; ask for clear amortized token cost delta between A100/H100 sizes.
SLA negotiation points: want 99.95% uptime for Dedicated pools with credit schedule; require defined remediation steps for latency SLO breaches (not just availability), on-call escalation matrix.
Security/compliance: EU data residency required for EU customers; SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning; KMS integration for key separation; retention controls for user messages (30/90/365 day options).
POC scope agreed: phase 1 load generator (synthetic traffic) + integration of request tracing; phase 2 realistic customer traffic replay (anonymized) + failover test; phase 3 SLA runbook review.
POC milestones: env build by Redwood (dedicated pool in us-east1 + eu-west1), smoke tests 2026-03-14, cross-region failover test 2026-03-24, final performance report 2026-04-02.
Risk notes: procurement has a list of preferred commercial terms (no indemnity carveouts); legal flagged EULA data residency clause; network egress cost sensitivity called out by infra finance.

Requested metrics/telemetry: token-level cost breakdown, per-model p50/p95 latency histograms, per-route throughput, token distribution by prompt length, eviction rates for KV cache.
Operational: want scheduled maintenance windows aligned to non-peak hours in each region; require advance notice 30 days for any disruptive maintenance on Dedicated pools.
Integration items: KMS proof-of-concept, SAML metadata exchange, SCIM group sync test, and audit log export to their SIEM (Splunk) — Redwood asked for sample schema and retention expectations.
